createAccount.summary: An account gives you a workspace — the private place your channels, posts and statistics live. Registration is the first step because everything else is attached to it.
createAccount.whenToUse: Once, before you start. If you already have an account, log in instead — you never repeat this step.
requirements: An email address you can open right now — the confirmation link goes there.
A password of at least 8 characters.
A name to display in WPoster. It can be your first name; it is not published anywhere.
steps: Open the registration page. If you are on the login page, use the “Register” link at the bottom.
Fill in Display Name. It is required and needs at least 2 characters. WPoster uses it to address you inside the app — it never appears in your posts.
Fill in Email. This becomes your login and receives the confirmation link, so use an address you can open now.
Fill in Password. The field asks for “Minimum 8 characters” — shorter passwords are refused and the form will not submit.
Complete the verification check that confirms you are not a bot.
Press “Register”. While the account is being created the button reads “Creating account...”.
You are taken to a screen titled “Check your email”. It shows the exact address the link was sent to, under “We've sent a confirmation link to:”.
outcomes: Your account is created.
The “Check your email” screen opens.
After you confirm, the Dashboard opens.
Your next step is connecting a platform.
createAccount.whatHappens: Until confirmed, the account exists but cannot sign in. On the Dashboard you will see the “Choose a platform” button — that is your next step.
tips: Register with an address you read every day. Support replies and announcements arrive inside WPoster, but the confirmation link only ever comes by email.
You do not need to create a workspace — one is made for you. Your next real decision is which channel to connect.

mistakes.problem: The Register button does nothing when pressed
mistakes.fix: One of the three required fields is empty or too short. Display Name needs 2 characters or more, and Password needs 8 — the browser highlights whichever field is blocking.

mistakes.problem: “An account with this email already exists”
mistakes.fix: You have registered with this address before. Use “Log in” instead, or “Forgot your password?” if you cannot remember it. Registering twice will not create a second account.

mistakes.problem: You registered but the login page keeps coming back
mistakes.fix: The account is not confirmed yet. Find the WPoster email and open its link — the next guide walks through it, including what to do when the email never arrives.

createAccount.goal: create your account and reach the Dashboard.

confirmEmail.summary: Prove the address is yours. Until you do, the account exists but you cannot get in.
confirmEmail.whenToUse: Right after registering. It takes one click and unlocks everything else.
steps: Look for the WPoster email in the inbox of the address you registered with. It arrives within a minute.
The “Check your email” screen shows exactly which address it went to. Compare it with what you expected — a typo is the usual reason nothing arrives.
Open the message and follow the confirmation link.
The link opens WPoster on a “Confirming your email” screen while it verifies.
When it finishes you see “Email confirmed” and a “Continue to WPoster” button.
Press it. You are logged in and land on the Dashboard.
tips: Confirmation links expire. If yours is old, register again with the same address to get a fresh one.
The link opens in whichever browser is your default. That is fine — WPoster logs you in there.
Once confirmed, you never do this again. Later sign-ins only need email and password.

mistakes.fix: Check spam and promotions folders first. Then re-read the address on the “Check your email” screen — if it has a typo, register again with the correct one.
The link was already used or is too old. Register again with the same address; a new link is sent.

mistakes.problem: The link opens the login page instead of confirming
mistakes.fix: The confirmation already went through. Just log in with your email and password.

confirmEmail.goal: confirm your email and sign in.

connectChannel.summary: Connect your first platform so WPoster has somewhere to publish.
connectChannel.whenToUse: Right after confirming your email. You cannot publish anything until at least one account is connected.
requirements: An account on the platform you want to publish to
Admin access to that channel or page
steps: Open the Dashboard — the first screen you see after signing in.
Press “Choose a platform”. It opens Settings → Connected Accounts, the hub for every platform.
In Connected Accounts, pick the platform you want to publish to — Telegram, Facebook, Instagram, X, Threads, Tumblr or Bluesky.
Press Connect and complete the connection. WPoster walks you through signing in or granting the access the platform needs.
When you finish, WPoster brings you back to Connected Accounts automatically — you never navigate back yourself.
A success message appears and the platform’s status turns to Connected.
From here connect another platform, or go straight to creating your first post.
outcomes: The account appears under Connected Accounts.
You can select it when you publish a post.
Analytics starts collecting data for it.
Your next step is creating your first post.
connectChannel.whatHappens: A connected account stays active until its access expires or you disconnect it. If the status ever shows Expired or Error, open it and press Reconnect.
tips: Use a work account you control — you will publish from it, so a throwaway is a bad idea.
Do not revoke WPoster’s access on the platform side. That flips the account to Expired and pauses publishing.
Check the status in Connected Accounts now and then; one Reconnect keeps a lapsed account live.

mistakes.problem: A social network will not connect
mistakes.fix: The authorization was probably cancelled — WPoster shows “Authorization was denied. Please try again.” Start Connect again and finish signing in.

mistakes.problem: Facebook shows no Pages to choose
mistakes.fix: WPoster reports “No Facebook Pages found. Make sure you are an admin of at least one Facebook Page.” Connect with an account that administers a Page.

mistakes.problem: The status shows Expired or Error
mistakes.fix: The platform’s access has lapsed. Open the account in Connected Accounts and press Reconnect — no need to remove and re-add it.

createPost.summary: Write your first post in the editor and publish it, schedule it or save it as a draft.
createPost.whenToUse: Once you have connected a channel. This is where every post starts.
requirements: Something to say — text, an image or a video
steps: Open the editor. Press “Create Post” at the top of WPoster.
Under “Publish to”, click the chip for the platform you connected — Telegram, Facebook, Instagram, X, Threads, Tumblr or Bluesky. Expand it and pick the channel or account.
Optionally give the post an internal title. It is used only inside WPoster to find posts later and is never published.
Write your post in the editor. WPoster formats it for each destination automatically.
Add images or a video if you want. The preview panel beside the editor shows exactly how the post will look on each platform.
Choose what happens next: “Publish Now” to send it immediately, “Schedule” to set a date and time, or “Save as Draft” to finish later.
outcomes: Your post is created — published, scheduled or saved as a draft.
It shows up in Posts with its status.
A published post starts collecting analytics.
Your next step is scheduling a publication.
createPost.whatHappens: A draft waits in Posts until you publish or schedule it. A scheduled post goes out automatically at the time you set, and you can edit it until then.
tips: The internal title is only for you — it helps you find posts later and never appears in what you publish.
Watch the preview panel as you type; it shows each platform’s formatting, so surprises show up before you publish.
Unsure? Press “Save as Draft” — nothing goes out until you choose “Publish Now” or “Schedule”.

mistakes.problem: I pressed Publish and nothing happened
mistakes.fix: No destination is selected. WPoster shows “Select at least one publishing destination.” — pick one under “Publish to”, then publish.

mistakes.problem: There are no platforms under “Publish to”
mistakes.fix: No account is connected yet. Open Connected Accounts, connect a platform, then return to the editor — its chip appears under “Publish to”.

mistakes.problem: An image or video will not upload
mistakes.fix: WPoster shows “Image upload failed. Please try again.” or “Image file is too large.” Use a smaller file and try again.

createPost.goal: write a post and publish, schedule or save it.

schedulePost.summary: Set a date and time and let WPoster publish the post for you.
schedulePost.goal: queue a post to publish at a time you choose.
schedulePost.whenToUse: When you want a post to go out later — at a better time, or while you are away.
requirements: A post you are ready to queue
steps: Open the editor and prepare your post — choose destinations under “Publish to” and write it, just like an immediate post.
Instead of “Publish Now”, choose “Schedule”.
This reveals “Scheduling Settings”. Set the “Schedule date” and “Schedule time” — WPoster reads them in your workspace timezone, shown as “Current timezone”.
Pick a date and time in the future, leaving enough lead time for the post to go out.
Confirm. You see “Post scheduled successfully” and the post is queued.
Open the Calendar to see it in the queue, or find it in Posts with the status Scheduled.
outcomes: The post is queued with the status Scheduled.
It appears on the Calendar at its date and time.
WPoster publishes it automatically — you need not be online.
Your next step is your first publication.
schedulePost.whatHappens: A scheduled post stays editable until it goes out. At the set time WPoster publishes it to every destination you chose.
tips: Check “Current timezone” before you confirm — the time is read in your workspace timezone, not the platform’s.
Use the Calendar to see your whole queue at a glance and spot gaps or clashes.
Not ready to commit to a time? Choose “Save as Draft” and schedule it later.

mistakes.problem: I can't find where to set the time
mistakes.fix: Choose “Schedule” first — it reveals “Scheduling Settings” with “Schedule date” and “Schedule time”. Set both there.

mistakes.problem: “Please select a publication date.” or “Please select a publication time.”
mistakes.fix: Both fields are required to schedule. Fill in the date and the time, then confirm.

mistakes.problem: The post published at the wrong hour
mistakes.fix: The time is read in your workspace timezone. Check “Current timezone”; to change it, go to Settings.

firstPublication.summary: Send your first post live and see the result across your channels.
firstPublication.goal: send a post live and read the result.
firstPublication.whenToUse: The moment you are ready to go public — the last step of setup.
requirements: A post with at least one destination
A minute to watch it go out
steps: In the editor, with your destinations chosen and your post written, choose “Publish Now”.
WPoster shows a “Publishing...” indicator, then sends the post to each channel.
Open Posts to see the result. Each post shows a status: Published or Failed.
The Dashboard reflects it too — the Published count rises and the post appears in recent activity.
If a destination fails, the Dashboard shows “N failed publications” with a “View failed posts” link.
Analytics begins collecting data for the published post.
outcomes: Your post is live on every destination that succeeded.
It shows the status Published in Posts.
The Dashboard and Analytics start reflecting it.
Setup is complete — you can now use WPoster fully.
firstPublication.whatHappens: Immediate and scheduled posts end the same way: Published when they go out, Failed if a platform rejects them. A scheduled post simply waits for its time.
tips: Publishing to several channels? One can fail while the rest succeed — check each post’s status, not just the first.
A “Failed” post keeps its content; open it, fix the cause and publish again.
The Dashboard’s failed-publications alert is the fastest way to catch a problem early.

mistakes.fix: One platform rejected the post. Open it from “View failed posts” on the Dashboard, check the reason, and publish again.

mistakes.problem: Some channels published and others did not
mistakes.fix: Multi-destination posts publish per channel. The successful ones are live; retry only the Failed ones from the post.

mistakes.problem: The post is not on the channel yet
mistakes.fix: If it is a scheduled post, it publishes at its set time, not now. Check the Calendar for the moment it goes out.
